# Feature Specification: VAT / Fiscal Receipt

**Feature ID:** 012-vat-fiscal-receipt
**Status:** Draft (SEED — generated by spec-seed workflow; NOT yet through /speckit-specify)
**Created:** 2026-06-07
**Last Updated:** 2026-06-07
**Owner:** (unassigned)

---

## Overview

> **BLOCKED — DO NOT PLAN OR IMPLEMENT.**
> This feature is gated on **Retail Tower gate G6 (fiscal model approval)**. There is no DP2
> fiscal/VAT contract today. The backend computes no VAT; the Connector currently drops
> `taxAmount` entirely. This spec cannot advance to `/speckit-clarify` or `/speckit-plan`
> until (a) G6 ratifies the Egyptian fiscal model and (b) a DP2 fiscal contract is published
> that POS-Pulse can consume. All FRs and scenarios below are behavioral placeholders only —
> no contract field names are assumed beyond the passive `tax_category` / `tax_amount` fields
> already carried verbatim on snapshot and sale rows.

Feature 008 (Sale Finalization & Receipts) ships an internal/dev MVP where `total_tax_minor`
is hardcoded to `0` and the printed receipt carries no tax line. Its §A5 sign-off explicitly
states that **customer-facing fiscal production use remains BLOCKED pending a future fiscal
feature** — this is that feature.

012 replaces the interim stub with real Egyptian VAT computation. It adds per-line VAT
breakdown to the receipt and a sale-level VAT total, sources the tenant's tax-registration
ID, and produces a fiscally-compliant printed receipt that satisfies Egyptian VAT obligations
for a pharmacy POS. ETA e-invoicing integration is a likely future extension but is
explicitly out of scope for v1.

POS-Pulse consumes **Data-Pulse-2 (DP2) contracts only**. It never calls ERPNext or Frappe
directly. The Retail-Tower-ERP-Next-Connector is the sole ERPNext speaker. ERPNext POS
Invoice (which carries a `taxes` table and Sales Taxes and Charges template) is **reference
only** — no ERPNext core code is copied.

---

## User Scenarios & Testing

### Primary User Story

As a **pharmacist / cashier** completing a taxable sale, I want the printed receipt to show
the correct VAT amount per line and a fiscally-compliant VAT total, so that the pharmacy can
hand customers a legally valid receipt and remain compliant with Egyptian VAT regulations.

### Acceptance Scenarios

**Given** a completed sale containing one or more items with a non-zero VAT rate sourced from
the DP2 fiscal contract,
**When** the cashier finalises the sale and prints a receipt,
**Then** the receipt displays: each line item with its unit price (ex-VAT), VAT rate, and
VAT amount in integer minor units; a sale-level subtotal (ex-VAT); a sale-level VAT total;
and a grand total (inc-VAT) — all amounts in integer minor units, never floats.

**Given** a sale where all items are VAT-exempt (zero-rated or exempt classification),
**When** the cashier finalises the sale and prints a receipt,
**Then** the receipt shows a VAT line of EGP 0.00, the tax-exempt classification is noted,
and no tax registration ID obligation is triggered for that line.

**Given** a sale in an offline state (no connectivity to DP2),
**When** the cashier finalises the sale,
**Then** the terminal applies the VAT rates last cached in the local snapshot and prints the
receipt with those rates; a staleness indicator is shown if the snapshot exceeds the
configured freshness threshold.

### Edge Cases

- Sale containing a mix of VAT-rated and VAT-exempt line items: receipt splits VAT summary
  by rate bucket; zero-rated lines appear in their own section.
- Rounding: VAT is computed per-line in integer minor units; any distributable remainder
  is allocated to the last applicable line (no float arithmetic at any point).
- Tenant tax-registration ID absent from the DP2 contract: receipt prints without the ID
  and a warning is written to the application log (no PII in log output).
- Receipt printer offline: sale is still persisted locally with the full VAT breakdown;
  receipt can be reprinted when the printer is available.

---

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

**FR-1.** The terminal must compute VAT for each sale line item using the VAT rate sourced
from the DP2 fiscal contract snapshot; computation uses integer minor units only (no floats).

**FR-2.** The printed receipt must display, for each line item: description, quantity, unit
price excluding VAT (minor units), applicable VAT rate (percentage), and VAT amount (minor
units).

**FR-3.** The printed receipt must display a sale-level summary section containing:
subtotal excluding VAT, total VAT (aggregated by rate bucket), and grand total including VAT.

**FR-4.** The tenant's tax-registration ID (sourced from DP2) must appear in the receipt
header when present.

**FR-5.** VAT-exempt and zero-rated items must be classified and displayed distinctly from
standard-rated items on the receipt.

**FR-6.** The local SQLite schema must persist the per-line VAT breakdown (rate, VAT amount
minor units, classification) alongside each sale line, replacing the current hardcoded
`total_tax_minor = 0` field in the sale record.

**FR-7.** The cashier must be able to reprint any historical receipt with the VAT breakdown
as originally computed at the time of sale (no recomputation at reprint time).

**FR-8.** All VAT data consumed by the terminal must arrive exclusively via DP2 contracts;
the terminal must never call ERPNext, Frappe, or any Connector endpoint directly.

**FR-9.** When the fiscal snapshot is stale beyond the configured freshness threshold, the
terminal must surface a staleness warning to the operator before allowing a taxable sale to
proceed; the operator may override with an explicit acknowledgement (logged, no PII).

**FR-10.** PII and cardholder data must never appear in application logs; VAT-related log
entries must be restricted to amounts, rate codes, and classification labels.

### Non-Functional Requirements

**NFR-1.** VAT computation for a 20-line sale must complete in under 5 ms on the target
hardware (LENOVO 82K2 / Ryzen 7 5800H class) — local arithmetic only, no IPC round-trip
required for computation.

**NFR-2.** The fiscal receipt layout must remain within the character width supported by the
target printer (BIXOLON SRP-330 II, 80 mm / 42-column text mode).

**NFR-3.** Test coverage on the VAT computation module must be >= 95 % (matching the money
module standard).

---

## Success Criteria

**SC-1.** A completed taxable sale produces a receipt where the sum of per-line VAT amounts
equals the printed sale-level VAT total (no rounding gap > 1 minor unit).

**SC-2.** The `total_tax_minor` field on the sale record in SQLite is no longer hardcoded to
`0`; it reflects the actual VAT collected for the transaction.

**SC-3.** Receipts for zero-rated and exempt items carry the correct classification label and
a VAT amount of `0` with no rounding residual.

**SC-4.** The VAT computation module achieves >= 95 % Vitest coverage before any integration
work begins (test-first).

**SC-5.** The printed receipt is accepted as fiscally valid by the tenant's accountant review
(manual sign-off criterion; deferred to §A5 of this feature).

**SC-6.** No float arithmetic appears anywhere in the VAT computation path (enforced by lint
rule or static assertion in tests).

---

## Key Entities

- **Sale** — existing 008 entity; extended with a populated `total_tax_minor` field and a
  per-line VAT breakdown sub-record.
- **SaleLine** — existing 008 entity; extended with `vat_rate_bps` (basis points),
  `vat_amount_minor` (integer), and `vat_classification` (standard / zero-rated / exempt).
- **FiscalSnapshot** — new local read model (design TBD post-G6); caches the DP2 fiscal/VAT
  contract data (rates, classifications, tenant tax-registration ID) alongside the catalogue
  snapshot.
- **TenantFiscalProfile** — logical entity sourced from DP2; carries the tenant
  tax-registration ID and applicable VAT scheme. Field names are **unknown until the DP2
  fiscal contract is published**.
- **Receipt** — existing 008 printed artefact; extended with per-line VAT columns and a
  multi-bucket VAT summary section.

---

## Assumptions

1. Egyptian VAT rates and classification rules will be delivered by DP2 as part of a
   fiscal contract ratified under G6; the terminal will not hard-code any rate values.
2. The target printer (BIXOLON SRP-330 II) supports the character width required for a
   per-line VAT column without a second receipt format.
3. ETA e-invoicing (Egypt Tax Authority electronic invoice mandate) is a likely future
   extension but does not constrain the v1 fiscal receipt format.
4. A single VAT scheme per tenant is sufficient for v1; multi-scheme (e.g. special economic
   zone rates) is out of scope.
5. The DP2 fiscal contract will expose a `tax_category` and a computed (not dropped)
   `tax_amount` field once G6 is ratified; the current Connector behaviour (dropping
   `taxAmount`) is a pre-G6 stub.

---

## Out of Scope

- ETA e-invoicing / electronic invoice submission to the Egyptian Tax Authority.
- Multi-VAT-scheme support within a single tenant or sale.
- VAT refund / credit note flows.
- ESC/POS fiscal printer integration beyond the existing 008 OS-print path.
- Any ERPNext Sales Taxes and Charges template logic — reference only, not implemented here.
- Inventory valuation tax or purchase-side VAT (input tax credit).
- Auto-update of VAT rates without an explicit catalogue refresh (rates travel with the
  snapshot; the operator triggers refresh via `catalogue:refresh`).

---

## Dependencies

> **HARD BLOCKER — first dependency below gates the entire feature.**

1. **[BLOCKED] Retail Tower gate G6 (fiscal model approval) + DP2 fiscal/VAT contract.**
   There is no DP2 fiscal/VAT contract today. The Connector currently drops `taxAmount`
   entirely. This feature cannot be designed, planned, or implemented until G6 is ratified
   and a DP2 fiscal contract is published. All other dependencies below are contingent.

2. **Feature 008 — Sale Finalization & Receipts** (merged). 012 extends 008's sale schema
   and receipt renderer; 008 must be fully merged and stable before 012 begins implementation.

3. **Feature 010 — Catalogue Read-Down Consumption** (in progress). The fiscal snapshot
   is expected to travel alongside or be appended to the catalogue snapshot; the
   `catalogue:refresh` IPC surface and the sync-state infrastructure introduced by 010 are
   the likely delivery mechanism for fiscal rate data.

4. **Feature 009 — Product Search & Barcode Lookup** (merged). Per-line VAT computation
   requires the `tax_category` field on each matched product; 009 owns the product read
   model and lookup path.

5. **DP2 fiscal contract (unknown shape).** Field names, rate encoding, classification
   vocabulary, and tenant tax-registration ID location are all unknown until the contract is
   published. No field names are assumed in this spec.

## Open Questions

1. **[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: G6 timeline and DP2 fiscal contract shape.]**
   When is Retail Tower gate G6 expected to be ratified, and what will the DP2 fiscal
   contract expose? Specifically: how are VAT rates encoded (basis points? percentage?),
   what classification vocabulary is used (standard / zero-rated / exempt / other?), and
   where does the tenant tax-registration ID live in the contract?

2. **[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: fiscal snapshot delivery mechanism.]**
   Will fiscal rate data travel as part of the existing catalogue snapshot (extending the
   010 `catalogue:refresh` flow) or as a separate DP2 endpoint with its own sync cadence?
   The answer determines whether 012 needs new IPC channels or can piggyback on 010's
   infrastructure.

3. **[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: ETA e-invoicing mandate applicability and timeline.]**
   Is ETA electronic invoice submission required for pharmacy POS transactions in the
   initial rollout scope, or is a printed fiscal receipt sufficient for v1? If required,
   what is the mandate date and does DP2 plan to provide an e-invoice submission contract?
